title: Elementary -Secondary Staff Information Reports

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Elementary -Secondary Staff Information Reports
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide, from the year 2017 to the present, all reports that CVUSD has submitted to the State of California or federal government, pursuant to the legal requirements found in 709(c) of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended, 42 U.S.C. 2000e-8(c), 29 CFR 1602.39 and .41-.45, and Cal. Gov’t Code § 8310.5. In summary, the above laws require school districts to report the racial/ethnic make up of teachers in the district, and are commonly known as EEO-5 reports. 

 This request seeks, from the year 2017 to the present, all reports (including but not limited to EEO-5 reports), spreadsheets, or other similar documents which CVUSD has given to the State of California or federal government, which reflects the racial and/or ethnic make up of teaching staff.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Annette Harings

I hope that this request has not been routed to a law firm who is dragging out responding as long as possible for some sort of strategic reason in an ongoing lawsuit.  That would be a shame.  

There is nothing that needs to be reviewed by a lawyer because these are simply reports that are given to other government entities.   There are no requested emails or communications.  It’s just reports.  

There should be nine responsive files total. One given to the state and federal government every year.  There is no privilege implicated because CVUSD already has the files and…sends it to the state/feds.  

Please ask Superintendent Frances Esparza where the records are.  Or ask the Board of Trustees where the documents are.  This should only take 10 minutes.   

I would hate to think a writ of mandate has to be filed to obtain these records.  Because if a writ is filed, and CVUSD subsequently produces documents, CVUSD has to pay attorneys fees and costs.  I know CVUSD has financial problems and I really don’t want to file a writ.   But this is truly a simple request and it consists of only 9 files.  
Thank you.  
Thanks.

Dear Traci Traci, I am writing in regard to Sunshine Request R024127-033126. After receiving your request it was provided to the relevant departments to begin their review. The City Clerk's office preliminary review has found multiple potentially responsive records among City Council meetings and that review is ongoing at this time. A full review of electronic calendar records will require a search to be conducted by Information Systems. We are working to obtain a time quote for this portion of your request. Until said search is conducted, we do not have a specific manner to identify meetings that may have been held throughout the City in regard to your request. Another option would require a search request to all departments and receiving their time quotes as necessary to address your request. Additionally, the majority of any records you may be seeking will be in the Custodianship of the Police Department. Unfortunately, the City Clerk’s office does not maintain Custodianship for Police Department records. To request Police Department responsive records, you will need to contact Crystal Higdon, who has been designated as their current Custodian. She may be reached via email at chigdon@springfieldmo.gov or via phone at 417-864-1814. Any additional questions regarding those records will need to be addressed to their Custodian. If you have any immediate questions, please feel free to respond to this message. Please look for an additional update in regard to your request on or about 13 April 2026. I look forward to further communication, Russ McLaughlin City Clerk Compliance Specialist City Clerk's Office

Dear Traci Traci, I am writing in regard to Sunshine Request R024127-033126. I apologize for the extensive delay that has been encountered with your request. As advised in our last message, the records collected for responsive review were provided by Information Services to the City Clerk's Office. At this time the City Clerk's office continues to address all received requests in as timely a fashion as possible. However, many requests we have received have included an Information Systems component similar to your own. These requests have generated multiple collections of documents resulting in tens of thousands of records in need of review. As such, we address them in the order received as possible with those individuals available to conduct the needed responsive review. This is a very time intensive process that must be conducted while maintaining all other duties any individual conducting review may be responsible for. I am happy to inform you that the collected records for the Information Systems portion of your request have passed through responsive review and a final review by Law to verify if any item might have been be closed or in need of redaction. We are now providing those records to you. At their discretion, the City Clerk has waived any additional fee for this portion of your request. communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

-the current term expiration date (month, day, and year) for each parole board member
-the annual salary / total compensation for each parole board member for 2026 

I am making this request for research purposes and am not a journalist.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Wourms

communications.subject: Request for Clarification - PRR-2025-0631
communications.communication:
Dear Moe K. Clark, This correspondence is to update you on your public records request. You requested the following: - Any and all lists, spreadsheets or other organized datasets that detail potential or substantiated allegations of misconduct and/or impeached or impeachable testimony, created under Brady v. Maryland and/or Giglio v. United States. 

- Any and all records regarding substantiated allegations of misconduct or violations of internal department policy or criminal law by specific law enforcement officers. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. This email is to seek clarification of your request. Our request for clarification is as follows: All Washington Brady-Giglio list, formally known as Potential Impeachment Disclosure (PID) under RCW 10.93.180, are required to be maintained by each individual law enforcement agency and reported to their county’s Prosecuting Attorney Office (PAO) within 10 days of an incident occurring. See RCW 10.93.180: Protocol for potential impeachment disclosures. There are 39 county prosecutors’ offices in Washington, and one of our divisions currently has about eleven lists in their possession but they may be outdated at this current juncture, and we are interpreting your request to be seeking the most up to date list. Nonetheless, we are more than happy to produce the limited materials we have but, if you are looking for the most accurate information available, you may want to contact the county prosecutors’ offices. Please let us know right away, but not later than October 3, 2025, if you wish to receive the approximate 11 lists. In addition, we have the following questions regarding the records you are seeking: 1.  may we apply a timeframe to your request? such as 2025? or the last year? 2.  may we apply a specific law enforcement agency? such as Olympia, WA Police Department or the Thurston County Sheriff's Department? Please let us know right away, but not later than October 3, 2025. If we do not hear from you on or before this date, we will begin producing records in installments as they come available. Please note that installments are provided free of charge via Box for inspection and/or download. You will not need a Box account to access the records. If you have any questions, please contact me via email or at Office of the Attorney General, Public Records & Constituent Services, P.O. Box 40100, Olympia, WA 98504-0100. Thank you. Sincerely, 
Bunny Archer Bunny Archer 
Public Records Officer & Constituent Correspondence Liaison 
Public Records & Constituent Services Unit 
Washington State Attorney General's Office 
PO Box 40100, Olympia, WA 98504-0100 
360-586-0725 | Bunny.Archer@atg.wa.gov

I have submitted the same request to the local agencies as well, so just seeking the lists in possession of the AG's office to compare with the local list.

Thank you!

Dear Moe K. Clark, This correspondence is to update you on your public records request. You requested the following: - Any and all lists, spreadsheets or other organized datasets that detail potential or substantiated allegations of misconduct and/or impeached or impeachable testimony, created under Brady v. Maryland and/or Giglio v. United States. 

- Any and all records regarding substantiated allegations of misconduct or violations of internal department policy or criminal law by specific law enforcement officers. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 
An installment of records responsive to your request has been uploaded to Box. The records consist of a 417-page document (MC - 00001 thru MC - 00417) with 16 (MB) of native data, as well as three Word documents and four Excel spreadsheets. You may inspect and/or download these records via this link: https://atg-wa.box.com/s/q7ht55gjm66e8xb0wxeqhpv0h2qdyj1g . Please do so within 30 days. Records provided via Box are free of charge. You do not need a Box account to access the records. If a password is required to access the records, one will be provided to you in a separate email. Also uploaded with these responsive documents is a key to the codes indicated as black boxes with a code, e.g., [1a], centered. The key identifies the statutory basis for the exemption as well as a brief explanation for why the exemption applies. As you review the responsive documents, you will be able to refer to the key to identify the exemption and its application. We have made every attempt to apply consistent redactions on documents that contain the same information. In the event you locate documents that contain redactions that are not applied consistently, please let me know. If you prefer to receive these records on CD, USB thumb drive, or paper, there is a charge. Please see the AGO Public Records Fee Schedule for cost information. If you prefer one of these formats, please submit a check or money order to my attention within 30 days, in the amount specified on the Fee Schedule, payable to the Office of the Attorney General, and send it to the address below. Once payment is received, the records will be mailed. Please be advised that if you do not either download these records, access them for inspection, or submit payment for an alternate format on or before December 3, 2025, the request is considered to have been fulfilled and is closed on that date for failure to claim or review records. This means that the Attorney General’s Office will not further address the request, and that is the date from which the Public Records Act’s one-year statute of limitations to seek judicial review starts to run. Please contact me within 30 days via email or at Office of the Attorney General, Public Records & Constituent Services, P.O. Box 40100, Olympia, WA 98504-0100, if you have any questions. Thank you. Sincerely, 
Bunny Archer 
Public Records Officer & Constituent Correspondence Liaison 
Public Records & Constituent Services Unit 
Washington State Attorney General's Office 
PO Box 40100, Olympia, WA 98504-0100 
360-586-0725 | Bunny.Archer@atg.wa.gov

You requested the following: - Any and all lists, spreadsheets or other organized datasets that detail potential or substantiated allegations of misconduct and/or impeached or impeachable testimony, created under Brady v. Maryland and/or Giglio v. United States. 

- Any and all records regarding substantiated allegations of misconduct or violations of internal department policy or criminal law by specific law enforcement officers. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 
An installment of records responsive to your request has been uploaded to Box. The records consist of a 192-page document (MC2-00001 - MC2-00192) and 8 MB of native data. You may inspect and/or download these records via this link: https://atg-wa.box.com/s/8uv751bc7nza93383zsc53otfz210x9b . Please do so within 30 days. Records provided via Box are free of charge. You do not need a Box account to access the records. If a password is required to access the records, one will be provided to you in a separate email. Also uploaded with these responsive documents is a key to the codes indicated as black boxes with a code, e.g., [1a], centered. The key identifies the statutory basis for the exemption as well as a brief explanation for why the exemption applies. As you review the responsive documents, you will be able to refer to the key to identify the exemption and its application. We have made every attempt to apply consistent redactions on documents that contain the same information. In the event you locate documents that contain redactions that are not applied consistently, please let me know. If you prefer to receive these records on CD, USB thumb drive, or paper, there is a charge. Please see the AGO Public Records Fee Schedule for cost information. If you prefer one of these formats, please submit a check or money order to my attention within 30 days, in the amount specified on the Fee Schedule, payable to the Office of the Attorney General, and send it to the address below. Once payment is received, the records will be mailed. Please be advised that if you do not either download these records, access them for inspection, or submit payment for an alternate format on or before June 11, 2026, the request is considered to have been fulfilled and is closed on that date for failure to claim or review records. This means that the Attorney General’s Office will not further address the request, and that is the date from which the Public Records Act’s one-year statute of limitations to seek judicial review starts to run. Please contact me within 30 days via email or at Office of the Attorney General, Public Records & Constituent Services, P.O. Box 40100, Olympia, WA 98504-0100, if you have any questions. Thank you. Sincerely, 
Bunny Archer

title: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Aberdeen School District 5 email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kung Fu Joe

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Kentucky Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request includes, without limitation, the following categories of records:
 
Bureau of Waste Site Cleanup (BWSC)
All records maintained by the Bureau of Waste Site Cleanup, including but not limited to Notices of Responsibility, Release Tracking Numbers (RTNs), Tier Classification Submittals, Phase I–V Comprehensive Site Assessments, Immediate Response Actions (IRAs), Release Abatement Measures (RAMs), Permanent Solution Statements, Activity and Use Limitations (AULs), Technical Assistance reports, environmental sampling data, laboratory analytical results, groundwater monitoring reports, soil and sediment sampling reports, vapor intrusion investigations, consultant reports, site inspection reports, enforcement actions, notices of noncompliance, and all related correspondence.
 
PFAS-Related Records
All records relating to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (“PFAS”), including investigations, sampling programs, analytical results, laboratory reports, notifications, questionnaires, audits, information requests, compliance reviews, permit reviews, enforcement actions, facility submissions, consultant reports, and correspondence concerning PFAS or fluorinated compounds.
 
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA)
All hazardous waste generator notification forms, annual and biennial reports, waste shipment manifests, exception reports, waste analyses, waste profiles, land disposal restriction notifications, transporter records, treatment, storage and disposal facility records, inspection reports, Notices of Violation (NOVs), administrative orders, enforcement actions, return-to-compliance documentation, and related correspondence.
 
National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) and Water Program Records
All permits, permit applications, engineering reports, site plans, drawings, maps, discharge monitoring reports (DMRs), monitoring data, correspondence, inspections, Notices of Violation, enforcement actions, return-to-compliance documentation, and records concerning industrial wastewater discharges, surface water discharges, groundwater discharges, infiltration systems, and stormwater discharges.
 
Industrial Pretreatment Program Records
All industrial user permits, wastewater discharge permits, pretreatment permits, self-monitoring reports, sampling results, inspection reports, enforcement actions, compliance evaluations, and correspondence concerning discharges to publicly owned treatment works (POTWs).
 
Stormwater Records
All stormwater permits, Notices of Intent, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), outfall maps, drainage plans, stormwater management plans, corrective action reports, inspection reports, monitoring data, benchmark monitoring reports, enforcement records, and correspondence.
 
Air Program Records
All air permits, permit applications, emissions inventories, source registrations, stack testing reports, compliance certifications, process descriptions, engineering drawings, inspection reports, enforcement records, and correspondence.
 
Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA)
All Tier II reports, Toxic Release Inventory (TRI) reports, Form R filings, hazardous chemical inventories, emergency response plans, Safety Data Sheets (SDSs/MSDSs), chemical inventory submissions, and related correspondence.
 
Spill and Release Records
All records concerning spills, releases, unauthorized discharges, emergency response actions, incident reports, notifications, cleanup activities, investigations, enforcement actions, and correspondence.
 
Process, Chemical Use, and Operational Records
All facility questionnaires, permit applications, process descriptions, manufacturing summaries, raw material inventories, chemical inventories, environmental audits, compliance certifications, engineering reports, environmental assessments, and related records describing manufacturing operations, products, chemicals, wastewater streams, emissions, waste generation, storage practices, disposal practices, pollution control systems, and environmental management activities.
 
Information Requests and Facility Responses
All information requests, questionnaires, surveys, audits, notices, compliance certifications, inquiries, and similar requests issued by MassDEP, together with all responses, submissions, attachments, and supporting materials provided by the facility.
 
Correspondence
All correspondence, including letters, emails, memoranda, meeting notes, meeting summaries, telephone logs, inspection notes, and communications between MassDEP personnel and the facility, its consultants, contractors, attorneys, owners, operators, or representatives concerning environmental compliance, contamination, investigations, PFAS, hazardous substances, wastewater, stormwater, groundwater, spills, waste management, or enforcement matters.
 
Historical Site Records
All historical aerial photographs, site plans, engineering drawings, drainage maps, utility maps, building plans, environmental assessments, closure reports, and records documenting historical operations, waste handling practices, disposal areas, lagoons, septic systems, dry wells, floor drains, underground storage tanks, aboveground storage tanks, wastewater treatment systems, and other potential contaminant release pathways.
 
PFAS-Specific Search Terms
For purposes of this request, records concerning PFAS include, but are not limited to, records referencing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, fluorinated surfactants, fluoropolymers, PTFE, Teflon®, FEP, PFA, ETFE, PVDF, PCTFE, fluorinated coatings, fluorinated processing aids, fluorinated lubricants, fluorochemical products, aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF), and any other fluorinated compounds used, stored, manufactured, discharged, disposed of, released, investigated, sampled, or discussed in connection with the facility.
 
Please provide responsive records in electronic format whenever available. If any portion of this request is denied or withheld, please identify the specific basis for withholding and provide an index describing the withheld records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nathan Byrd

title: Surveillance Cameras / ALPR Systems (Flock Safety) – Town of Fishkill

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: FOIL Request – Surveillance Cameras / ALPR Systems (Flock Safety) – Town of Fishkill
communications.communication:
Dear Records Custodian,

Under the provisions of the New York Freedom of Information Law (FOIL), N.Y. Public Officers Law §§ 84–90, I hereby request access to and copies of records held by the Town of Fishkill, Dutchess County, relating to the planning, proposal, procurement, authorization, or attempted deployment of Flock Safety surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems.

This request is made in the public interest to better understand the use, consideration, or implementation of surveillance technologies by local government entities, including decision-making processes, vendor relationships, and potential impacts on public privacy.

The purpose of this request is to determine the origin, authorization process, procurement activity, proposed locations, and communications surrounding any surveillance camera system, including identifying which individual, agency, or vendor first initiated discussions or planning for such a program within the Town of Fishkill.

Timeframe: January 1, 2023 – Present, including any earlier records referencing or relating to Flock Safety, automated license plate readers, or surveillance cameras within the Town of Fishkill.

Records Requested

For the purpose of this request, the records I seek include, but are not limited to the following:

1. Contracts and Agreements

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, vendor agreements, procurement documents, or proposals involving the Town of Fishkill and Flock Safety or any related entities concerning surveillance cameras, automated license plate readers, or related monitoring technology.

This includes draft contracts, executed agreements, amendments, pilot program agreements, trial program documentation, cancellation notices, procurement justifications, and contract termination records.

Legal Basis: Contracts involving public funds or public infrastructure are public records subject to disclosure under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87.

2. Records Identifying Project Initiation

All records reflecting the initial introduction, proposal, solicitation, or outreach regarding Flock Safety cameras or ALPR systems, including records identifying:

• the individual or office that first proposed or recommended the system  
• the first communications between the Town and Flock Safety  
• vendor outreach to town officials  
• internal discussions about introducing the technology  
• marketing or sales outreach from vendors  

3. Internal Communications

All internal communications including emails, memoranda, text messages, chat messages, letters, meeting notes, or other correspondence among:

• the Town Supervisor  
• Town Board members  
• Town of Fishkill Police Department personnel  
• Town administrative staff  
• Town legal counsel  
• Highway or Building Department personnel  
• other municipal offices  

that discuss:

• Flock Safety  
• automated license plate readers  
• surveillance cameras  
• camera deployments  
• vendor procurement or negotiations  
• surveillance technology adoption  

4. Communications With External Entities

All communications between the Town of Fishkill and:

• representatives of Flock Safety  
• technology vendors or consultants  
• Dutchess County officials  
• local, state, or federal law enforcement agencies  
• regional intelligence or real-time crime centers  

concerning surveillance cameras, ALPR systems, or the Flock Safety program.

5. Vendor Demonstrations and Sales Outreach

All records relating to vendor presentations, product demonstrations, marketing materials, or sales outreach regarding Flock Safety or related surveillance technology, including:

• presentation decks  
• vendor proposals  
• demonstration scheduling emails  
• meeting invitations or call summaries  
• webinar invitations  
• follow-up communications  

6. Proposed Camera Locations and Site Selection

All records identifying, evaluating, or discussing proposed or potential locations for surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader systems within the Town of Fishkill.

This includes but is not limited to:

• maps showing proposed camera placements  
• GIS maps or infrastructure maps  
• deployment plans  
• proposed installation locations or intersections  
• roadway monitoring points  
• entry or exit routes to the town  
• communications discussing site selection  
• vendor recommendations for placement  
• field surveys or site inspections  
• infrastructure or engineering assessments related to camera placement  

7. Deployment and Planning Documents

All planning or operational records relating to the surveillance system, including:

• deployment plans  
• camera location maps  
• infrastructure assessments  
• equipment specifications  
• installation schedules  
• operational capability descriptions  
• technology architecture documents  

8. Financial and Procurement Records

All records relating to funding, budgeting, or procurement of the surveillance system, including:

• invoices  
• payment records  
• purchase authorizations  
• budget allocations  
• grant applications  
• cost analyses  
• procurement justifications  
• financial approvals  

9. Meeting Records

All agendas, minutes, recordings, transcripts, or notes from Town Board meetings, committee meetings, departmental meetings, or internal meetings where surveillance camera programs or Flock Safety systems were discussed, proposed, approved, or canceled.

10. Oversight, Audit, and Compliance Records

Any audit reports, legal opinions, compliance reviews, investigations, or internal analyses relating to surveillance camera programs or procurement processes.

11. Data Access, Sharing, and Integration

All records relating to data access or sharing involving the surveillance system, including:

• agreements allowing other agencies to access camera data  
• policies governing license plate reader searches  
• records concerning integration with regional surveillance networks  
• data retention policies  
• privacy or civil liberties assessments  

Electronic Records and Metadata

For all responsive electronic records, including emails and digital documents, I request that records be produced in their native electronic format where possible, including all available metadata and email header information.

This includes, but is not limited to:

• sender and recipient information  
• CC and BCC fields  
• full email header routing data  
• timestamps for sending and receipt  
• message ID fields  
• attachment metadata  
• document creation dates  
• last modified dates  
• author fields  
• file path information where available  

Providing metadata is necessary to determine the origin, timing, and authorship of communications relating to the surveillance camera proposal.

Request for Segregable Non-Exempt Portions

Should any portion of the requested records be deemed exempt from disclosure, I request the release of any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions in accordance with N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87(2).

Preservation of Records

Please note your obligation not to destroy or alter any records potentially responsive to this request. Once a FOIL request has been received, agencies are required to preserve all responsive records during processing.

Fee Waiver Request

I request a fee waiver for the processing of this request as the information sought is in the public interest and its disclosure will contribute significantly to public understanding of government surveillance programs and decision-making processes.

If potential fees exceed $200, please inform me before proceeding.

Public Availability of Communications

Please be advised that communications relating to this request, including incoming and outgoing correspondence, may be publicly published on transparency platforms such as MuckRock.com.

Statutory Response Time

As required under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 89(3), I look forward to acknowledgment of this request within five business days.

Sincerely,

Jordan Lassiter  
Independent Investigative Journalist

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arizona Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The following materials regarding the imposition, assessment, collection and balances of inmate fees and debt:

a) All current policies and procedures regarding medical copays and room & board costs or fees for which inmates  are or may become liable. Sincerely,

Jenny Wadhwa

communications.subject: Louisiana Public Records Law Request: KFF Health News Immediate Jeopardy Records Request, Louisiana
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Louisiana Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records from Jan. 1, 2020, 
to the date of production of records responsive to this request that include the following:

• All notification letters sent from state agencies to CMS recommending Immediate 
Jeopardy for all Louisiana hospitals only during the above specified period. 
Please include letters that are sent directly to hospital administrations with a 
carbon copied email to CMS staff. You will find attached to this request an example 
of the kind of record I’m requesting.

• All letters from CMS to all Louisiana hospital administrators or other leadership 
staff notifying the finding of immediate jeopardy and the intent to terminate the 
CMS/provider agreement and during the above specified period. You will find 
attached to this request an example of the kind of record I’m requesting.

• All letters from CMS to all Louisiana hospital administrators or other leadership 
staff at hospitals announcing the involuntary termination of the CMS/provider 
agreement. You will find attached to this request an example of the kind of record 
I’m requesting.

Please provide these files in digital format by email or digital download. 

I am a journalist with KFF Health News and I'm seeking these records for reporting, not for any commercial use.

Note that a previous version of this request which is now closed made the same request. The response from the agency stated, "The request does not identify any records specifically sought from LDH." On the contrary, all the records sought in this request specify hospitals in the state of Louisiana, which LDH has a part in regulating.

I am requesting letters in the possession of LDH, regardless of whether they were created by CMS. Additionally, letters that LDH created informing CMS of immediate jeopardy are created by LDH. 

All these communications are in the possession of LDH and I am requesting them. 

If there is confusion about what the letters are, please refer to the attachments on this request. 

To be clear, this is a request to the Louisiana Department of Health for records on hospitals that it regulates. Because it regulates those hospitals, especially in respect to surveys and findings of immediate jeopardy, the records should be in the possession of LDH. 

If they are not in the possession of LDH, please explain why and point me to the agency that is the custodian of those records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Jones

Please be advised that the Centers for Medicaid & Medicare Services (CMS) is the custodian of records for all letters issued by CMS, including those which you have requested, under applicable law. Moreover, the letters issued by CMS to which the Louisiana Department of Health does have access through the federal certification database maintained by CMS are drafts of CMS letters only that must be requested from CMS through the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). Therefore, "all letters from CMS to all Louisiana hospital administrators or other leadership staff..." as you have requested may not be disclosed by the Louisiana Department of Health as public records under the Louisiana Public Records Law, La. R.S. 44:1 et seq. 
It is recommended that you submit a FOIA request to CMS for "all letters from CMS to all Louisiana hospital administrators or other leadership staff" to obtain those documents. 
Sincerely, 
Ryan Romero 
Bureau of Legal Services (BLS) 
Louisiana Department of Health

communications.communication:
--- Please respond above this line --- 

RE: Health Standards Section Records Request of September 09, 2026, Reference # P006511-090926 
Dear Andrew Jones, 
The Louisiana Department of Health received a records request from you on September 09, 2026. Your request mentioned: “To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Louisiana Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records: 

I am requesting an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records from Jan. 1, 2020, 
to the date of production of records responsive to this request that include the following: 

• All notification letters sent from state agencies to CMS recommending Immediate 
Jeopardy for all Louisiana hospitals only during the above specified period. 
Please include letters that are sent directly to hospital administrations with a 
carbon copied email to CMS staff. You will find attached to this request an example 
of the kind of record I’m requesting. 

• All letters from CMS to all Louisiana hospital administrators or other leadership 
staff notifying the finding of immediate jeopardy and the intent to terminate the 
CMS/provider agreement and during the above specified period. You will find 
attached to this request an example of the kind of record I’m requesting. 

• All letters from CMS to all Louisiana hospital administrators or other leadership 
staff at hospitals announcing the involuntary termination of the CMS/provider 
agreement. You will find attached to this request an example of the kind of record 
I’m requesting. 

Please provide these files in digital format by email or digital download. 

I am a journalist with KFF Health News and I'm seeking these records for reporting, not for any commercial use. 

Note that a previous version of this request which is now closed made the same request. The response from the agency stated, "The request does not identify any records specifically sought from LDH." On the contrary, all the records sought in this request specify hospitals in the state of Louisiana, which LDH has a part in regulating. 

I am requesting letters in the possession of LDH, regardless of whether they were created by CMS. Additionally, letters that LDH created informing CMS of immediate jeopardy are created by LDH. 

All these communications are in the possession of LDH and I am requesting them. 

If there is confusion about what the letters are, please refer to the attachments on this request. 

To be clear, this is a request to the Louisiana Department of Health for records on hospitals that it regulates. Because it regulates those hospitals, especially in respect to surveys and findings of immediate jeopardy, the records should be in the possession of LDH. 

If they are not in the possession of LDH, please explain why and point me to the agency that is the custodian of those records. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Andrew Jones 

Attachments: 

https://cdn.muckrock.com/outbound_composer_attachments/ajoneskff/185102/TERMINATION_EXAMPLE.pdf 
https://cdn.muckrock.com/outbound_composer_attachments/ajoneskff/185102/FINDING_EXAMPLE.pdf 
https://cdn.muckrock.com/outbound_composer_attachments/ajoneskff/185102/SURVEY_EXAMPLE.pdf 
Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2394467/” 
The Department has reviewed its files and has located responsive records to your request. 
Please log in to the LDH Records Center at the following link to retrieve the appropriate responsive documents. Health Standards Section Records Request - P006511-090926 
If you have any questions, or wish to discuss this further, please contact me. 
Sincerely, 
Ryan Romero 
Louisiana Department of Health

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: SFPD Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Records Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

We request the following records related to Automated License Plate Readers ("ALPRs") and your law enforcement agency ("Agency").

Part A - Information related to ALPR data sharing.

A1. The names of agencies and organizations with which the Agency shared ALPR data in 2025;

A2. The names of agencies and organizations from which the Agency received ALPR data in 2025;

A3. The names of agencies and organizations with which the Agency shares “hot list” information in 2025;

A4. The names of agencies and organizations from which the Agency receives “hot list” information in 2025.

The information requested in items A1-A4 is readily available for extraction through the ALPR software you use. For example, with Vigilant Solutions/Motorola Solutions, this data can be exported easily using the Data Sharing Report function. With Flock Safety, this information is available through the transparency portal function. 

Most agencies have encountered little difficulty in providing this information (see below). In a small number of cases, an agency has interpreted items A1-A4 as requesting the creation of a record that does not exist. We disagree: this data is maintained by your software, can be exported through software your agency has already purchased, and is therefore subject to CPRA.

However, should you disagree, you may alternatively produce the following records:

A5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, requests, or other certifying documents that external agencies have signed to comply with Sec 1798.90.52(b) for accessing your agency's ALPR data. These documents are also often required under the "Releasing ALPR Data" subsection of a California law enforcement agency's SB 34 policy.

A6. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, requests, or other certifying documents that your agency has signed pursuant to Sec 1798.90.52(b) to access other agencies' ALPR data.

A7. All "records of access" required by Sec. 1798.90.52(a) for the periods May 28th, 2024 until the date of processing this request.

Items A5-A7 are not necessary if your agency provides the information requested in items A1-A4. We feel that items A1-A4 are more focused and would require less labor from your agency to produce.

Part B - Information Related to Numbers of “Detections” (plate scans) and “Hits” (plate scans that matched to a hotlist)

B1. The aggregate number of "detections" collected during 2025.

B2. The aggregate number of “hits” during 2025.

B3. The aggregate number of "detections" from May 28th, 2024 until the date this request is processed. If your agency has a retention period shorter than 1 year, please provide whatever data is available based on your retention period. For example, most Flock Safety systems may not have this data beyond 30 days.

B4. The aggregate number of “hits” from May 28th, 2024 until the date this request is processed. If your agency has a retention period shorter than 1 year, please provide whatever data is available based on your retention period.

B5. Average Daily Scans based on the past amount of days in which you retain data.

The information requested in items B1-B4 is readily available through the ALPR software you use. For example, with Vigilant Solutions/Motorola Solutions, this data can be exported easily using the Hit Ratio Report function. With Flock Safety, this information is available through the transparency portal function. As noted above, this information exists within your system and can be easily exported with existing software.

Part C - Assistance, Description, and Recommendations.

We make the following requests under section 6253.1 of the California Public Records Act

C1. A description of the information technology and physical location in which the records exist.

C2. Assist us identifying records and information that will help the public understand how ALPR data and hotlists are shared, how much data is collected year-to-year, and how much of that data matches a hot list; and

C3. Provide suggestions for overcoming any practical basis for denying access to the information sought.

Please note that more than 80 California law enforcement agencies have provided the information requested in Parts A1-A4 and B1-B4 in previous years. For your reference we have included a PDF below with the names of the agencies that have historically provided these records.

(This URL links to a dataset with links to the records: https://www.eff.org/document/data-driven-2-california-dragnet-data-set)

Part D - Information Related to New Changes 

D1. Flock Safety has announced that they are building a product called Flock Nova, which utilizes information from people lookup tools, data brokers, and data breaches. It is mentioned in this article (https://www.404media.co/license-plate-reader-company-flock-is-building-a-massive-people-lookup-tool-leak-shows/) that the tool is being used by some law enforcement agencies in an early access program (https://www.flocksafety.com/devices/flock-nova#:~:text=Flock%20Nova%20Early%20Access%20Now%20Open). Is/has your Agency utilized Flock Nova? If yes, have you used the tool in any police investigations?

D2. Please send a document of the most up-to-date ALPR policy that your Agency uses.

Part E – Information Related to ALPR Camera Locations

E1. The location (address, intersection, coordinates, or nearest landmark) of each ALPR camera operated, maintained, or accessed by the Agency as of the date of this request.

E2. If your agency uses mobile ALPR cameras (e.g., on patrol cars), please indicate how many mobile units are currently deployed, and describe any policies that govern how locations of scans from mobile units are logged or stored.

E3. If exact addresses or coordinates are withheld, please provide general placement descriptions (e.g., "fixed camera at Main St & 2nd Ave," or "mobile ALPR unit assigned to Northern District patrol vehicle").

This information is typically accessible within ALPR system management software. For example:

- In Flock Safety camera location information is visible through the camera dashboard and deployment maps.
- In Vigilant/Motorola, camera locations are often listed in the device management or configuration settings.

Part F - ALPR Vendor Contracts and Purchase Agreements

F1. All contracts, purchase orders, service agreements, statements of work, or memoranda of understanding between the Agency and any vendor of ALPR technology (including Flock Safety, Vigilant Solutions/Motorola, etc.) in effect during 2024–2025.

F2. All invoices, receipts, and payment records related to the purchase, installation, operation, or maintenance of ALPR systems during 2024–2025.

F3. Any grant applications or grant award documents (e.g., from DHS, DOJ, or private foundations) that funded or supported the acquisition or expansion of ALPR systems.

Part G – Internal Communications and Rationale for Placement

G1. Any internal memos, emails, reports, or presentations from 2022–2025 discussing where ALPR cameras should be placed or were ultimately placed. This includes communications from officers, command staff, city officials, or vendor representatives regarding:

- Placement location recommendations
- Crime statistics or justifications used to determine placement
- Community concerns or opposition
- Equity or privacy impacts
- “High crime” area designations or related targeting rationale

G2. Any communications with Flock Safety, Vigilant Solutions, or other ALPR vendors from 2022–2025 regarding camera placement, pilot programs, early access programs, or system expansion.

CPRA requires you to undertake reasonable efforts to locate responsive records and to work in good faith with requesters to respond to their request. See CYAC v. City of National City, 220 Cal.App.4th 1385, 1430 (2013). Thus under the CPRA you are obligated to conduct a reasonable search and cannot deny a request merely because it might generate a large volume of records.

We ask that you please respond to this request within 10 days either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority on which you rely in withholding or redacting any document, as well as stating when documents will be made available. Should you choose to withhold or reject this request, we ask that you provide an explanation of why your agency is responding differently compared to the many others that have complied with our request.

Part H – ALPR Audit Logs & Access Records (More Detail)

H1. A list of all ALPR database users employed by the Agency between Jan 1, 2024 and the present, including job titles, divisions, and access levels.

H2. Audit logs showing ALPR database access by Agency personnel from Jan 1, 2024 to the present. Please include:

- Date and time of access
- Name and Job Title of User
- Search parameters (e.g., plate number or geographic query)
- Stated reason for access, if logged

These logs are required under California Civil Code § 1798.90.52(a) and can help determine how often ALPR data is being queried and by whom. These records have been disclosed by several agencies in prior CPRA requests.

If the records responsive to any part of this request are held by another department, division, or city office (such as the Mayor’s Office, Department of Technology, SFMTA, or a surveillance oversight board), please identify the appropriate custodian or refer this request accordingly, as required under Government Code § 6253.1.

In particular, if your agency does not maintain records related to:

- The policy rationale or decision-making process for camera placement
- Contracts or procurement related to ALPR vendors
- Surveillance technology policy

Please inform me which department or office may hold these records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

If good cause exists, reports shall be released no later than ten (10) working days after the request is made. 
Your report is available for processing upon ID verification. Please send us a copy of your Valid Identification (any current ID, including a valid driver's license, SF City ID card, a State-Issued ID card or a Passport (originating country Ok). Your request will be processed upon receipt.

communications.subject: San Francisco Police Public Records Request :: P277213-100626
communications.communication:
Dear Omar Solis: 
 
Thank you for your interest in public records of the San Francisco Police Department ("SFPD"). 
 
The San Francisco Police Department ("SFPD") received your request, dated October 06, 2026 and given the reference number P277213-100626 for tracking purposes. 
 
Record(s) Requested: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records: 

We request the following records related to Automated License Plate Readers ("ALPRs") and your law enforcement agency ("Agency"). 

Part A - Information related to ALPR data sharing. 

A1. The names of agencies and organizations with which the Agency shared ALPR data in 2025; 

A2. The names of agencies and organizations from which the Agency received ALPR data in 2025; 

A3. The names of agencies and organizations with which the Agency shares “hot list” information in 2025; 

A4. The names of agencies and organizations from which the Agency receives “hot list” information in 2025. 

The information requested in items A1-A4 is readily available for extraction through the ALPR software you use. For example, with Vigilant Solutions/Motorola Solutions, this data can be exported easily using the Data Sharing Report function. With Flock Safety, this information is available through the transparency portal function. 

Most agencies have encountered little difficulty in providing this information (see below). In a small number of cases, an agency has interpreted items A1-A4 as requesting the creation of a record that does not exist. We disagree: this data is maintained by your software, can be exported through software your agency has already purchased, and is therefore subject to CPRA. 

However, should you disagree, you may alternatively produce the following records: 

A5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, requests, or other certifying documents that external agencies have signed to comply with Sec 1798.90.52(b) for accessing your agency's ALPR data. These documents are also often required under the "Releasing ALPR Data" subsection of a California law enforcement agency's SB 34 policy. 

A6. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, requests, or other certifying documents that your agency has signed pursuant to Sec 1798.90.52(b) to access other agencies' ALPR data. 

A7. All "records of access" required by Sec. 1798.90.52(a) for the periods May 28th, 2024 until the date of processing this request. 

Items A5-A7 are not necessary if your agency provides the information requested in items A1-A4. We feel that items A1-A4 are more focused and would require less labor from your agency to produce. 

Part B - Information Related to Numbers of “Detections” (plate scans) and “Hits” (plate scans that matched to a hotlist) 

B1. The aggregate number of "detections" collected during 2025. 

B2. The aggregate number of “hits” during 2025. 

B3. The aggregate number of "detections" from May 28th, 2024 until the date this request is processed. If your agency has a retention period shorter than 1 year, please provide whatever data is available based on your retention period. For example, most Flock Safety systems may not have this data beyond 30 days. 

B4. The aggregate number of “hits” from May 28th, 2024 until the date this request is processed. If your agency has a retention period shorter than 1 year, please provide whatever data is available based on your retention period. 

B5. Average Daily Scans based on the past amount of days in which you retain data. 

The information requested in items B1-B4 is readily available through the ALPR software you use. For example, with Vigilant Solutions/Motorola Solutions, this data can be exported easily using the Hit Ratio Report function. With Flock Safety, this information is available through the transparency portal function. As noted above, this information exists within your system and can be easily exported with existing software. 

Part C - Assistance, Description, and Recommendations. 

We make the following requests under section 6253.1 of the California Public Records Act 

C1. A description of the information technology and physical location in which the records exist. 

C2. Assist us identifying records and information that will help the public understand how ALPR data and hotlists are shared, how much data is collected year-to-year, and how much of that data matches a hot list; and 

C3. Provide suggestions for overcoming any practical basis for denying access to the information sought. 

Please note that more than 80 California law enforcement agencies have provided the information requested in Parts A1-A4 and B1-B4 in previous years. For your reference we have included a PDF below with the names of the agencies that have historically provided these records. 

(This URL links to a dataset with links to the records: https://www.eff.org/document/data-driven-2-california-dragnet-data-set) 

Part D - Information Related to New Changes 

D1. Flock Safety has announced that they are building a product called Flock Nova, which utilizes information from people lookup tools, data brokers, and data breaches. It is mentioned in this article (https://www.404media.co/license-plate-reader-company-flock-is-building-a-massive-people-lookup-tool-leak-shows/) that the tool is being used by some law enforcement agencies in an early access program (https://www.flocksafety.com/devices/flock-nova#:~:text=Flock%20Nova%20Early%20Access%20Now%20Open). Is/has your Agency utilized Flock Nova? If yes, have you used the tool in any police investigations? 

D2. Please send a document of the most up-to-date ALPR policy that your Agency uses. 

Part E – Information Related to ALPR Camera Locations 

E1. The location (address, intersection, coordinates, or nearest landmark) of each ALPR camera operated, maintained, or accessed by the Agency as of the date of this request. 

E2. If your agency uses mobile ALPR cameras (e.g., on patrol cars), please indicate how many mobile units are currently deployed, and describe any policies that govern how locations of scans from mobile units are logged or stored. 

E3. If exact addresses or coordinates are withheld, please provide general placement descriptions (e.g., "fixed camera at Main St & 2nd Ave," or "mobile ALPR unit assigned to Northern District patrol vehicle"). 

This information is typically accessible within ALPR system management software. For example: 

- In Flock Safety camera location information is visible through the camera dashboard and deployment maps. 
- In Vigilant/Motorola, camera locations are often listed in the device management or configuration settings. 

Part F - ALPR Vendor Contracts and Purchase Agreements 

F1. All contracts, purchase orders, service agreements, statements of work, or memoranda of understanding between the Agency and any vendor of ALPR technology (including Flock Safety, Vigilant Solutions/Motorola, etc.) in effect during 2024–2025. 

F2. All invoices, receipts, and payment records related to the purchase, installation, operation, or maintenance of ALPR systems during 2024–2025. 

F3. Any grant applications or grant award documents (e.g., from DHS, DOJ, or private foundations) that funded or supported the acquisition or expansion of ALPR systems. 

Part G – Internal Communications and Rationale for Placement 

G1. Any internal memos, emails, reports, or presentations from 2022–2025 discussing where ALPR cameras should be placed or were ultimately placed. This includes communications from officers, command staff, city officials, or vendor representatives regarding: 

- Placement location recommendations 
- Crime statistics or justifications used to determine placement 
- Community concerns or opposition 
- Equity or privacy impacts 
- “High crime” area designations or related targeting rationale 

G2. Any communications with Flock Safety, Vigilant Solutions, or other ALPR vendors from 2022–2025 regarding camera placement, pilot programs, early access programs, or system expansion. 

CPRA requires you to undertake reasonable efforts to locate responsive records and to work in good faith with requesters to respond to their request. See CYAC v. City of National City, 220 Cal.App.4th 1385, 1430 (2013). Thus under the CPRA you are obligated to conduct a reasonable search and cannot deny a request merely because it might generate a large volume of records. 

We ask that you please respond to this request within 10 days either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority on which you rely in withholding or redacting any document, as well as stating when documents will be made available. Should you choose to withhold or reject this request, we ask that you provide an explanation of why your agency is responding differently compared to the many others that have complied with our request. 

Part H – ALPR Audit Logs & Access Records (More Detail) 

H1. A list of all ALPR database users employed by the Agency between Jan 1, 2024 and the present, including job titles, divisions, and access levels. 

H2. Audit logs showing ALPR database access by Agency personnel from Jan 1, 2024 to the present. Please include: 

- Date and time of access 
- Name and Job Title of User 
- Search parameters (e.g., plate number or geographic query) 
- Stated reason for access, if logged 

These logs are required under California Civil Code § 1798.90.52(a) and can help determine how often ALPR data is being queried and by whom. These records have been disclosed by several agencies in prior CPRA requests. 

If the records responsive to any part of this request are held by another department, division, or city office (such as the Mayor’s Office, Department of Technology, SFMTA, or a surveillance oversight board), please identify the appropriate custodian or refer this request accordingly, as required under Government Code § 6253.1. 

In particular, if your agency does not maintain records related to: 

- The policy rationale or decision-making process for camera placement 
- Contracts or procurement related to ALPR vendors 
- Surveillance technology policy 

Please inform me which department or office may hold these records. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Omar Solis 

Upload documents directly: https://accounts.muckrock.com/accounts/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.muckrock.com%2Faccounts%2Flogin%2F%3Fnext%3D%252Faccounts%252Fagency_login%252Fsan-francisco-police-department-367%252Fsfpd-automated-license-plate-reader-alpr-records-request-187112%252F%253Femail%253Dsanfranciscopd%252540govqa.us&url_auth_token=AAAIhlqz_6HzFpF9QbtVNXCgHbA%3A1uKU5a%3ACMR8oK2B9iYvGyHaTwoLy9dNKeUTmPmihkLaiLJ5KUQ 
 
Your request is being forwarded to the appropriate department(s) for processing and you will be notified once the request is complete. 
 
You can monitor request progress at the link below.  Thank you for using the San Francisco Public Records Center. 
 
 
San Francisco Police Department

title: ALPR Policies, Sharing Settings, and System Configuration

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: ALPR Policies, Sharing Settings, and System Configuration
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records held by Plano Police Department concerning each automated license plate reader (ALPR) system it uses or has used since January 1, 2026, from any vendor, including the Flock Safety system and the Motorola Solutions VehicleManager system referenced in Administrative Directive 112.044. These records are generated within the ALPR systems, and standard system exports or screenshots of settings pages are sufficient. Where a record exists for more than one system, please provide it for each.

I am aware of request P057571-083026. I am not requesting the July 2024 version of Directive 112.044 or the Flock invoices already released under that request.

1. Any revision of Administrative Directive 112.044 adopted after July 27, 2024, and any directive or policy governing the department's drone program or its Real Time Information Center.
2. For each ALPR system, the current data sharing settings, including:
   a. Agencies or networks sharing ALPR data with the department (in Flock, "shared with me");
   b. Agencies or networks the department shares its ALPR data with (in Flock, "networks I'm sharing");
   c. Any statewide, out-of-state, national, or federal sharing that is enabled, including sharing with the Texas Department of Public Safety and any access by federal agencies such as ICE, CBP, HSI, DEA, or DHS, with the date each such setting was enabled or disabled.
3. Records showing, for each ALPR system, the number of fixed, vehicle-mounted, and deployable or trailer-mounted cameras operated by or on behalf of the department, and the location of each fixed camera.
4. Records showing each ALPR system's configured data retention period and any changes to it since the start of the contract.
5. Records showing whether the department has access to commercially collected LPR data (for example data collected by private companies and made available through a vendor), and any agreement governing that access.
6. A list of non-government ALPR or video camera sources accessible to the department through any ALPR system (for example cameras owned by homeowners associations, businesses, apartment complexes, or residents), by owner type and general location.
7. Existing reports or exports from each ALPR system showing, by month since January 1, 2026: the number of alerts generated, the number of alerts confirmed by an officer, and the number of alerts determined to be misreads or false positives.
8. Any ALPR transparency reports or usage summaries prepared by or for the department since January 1, 2025.
9. Records reflecting the 2026 deactivation of the department's Flock cameras and network access, including the date cameras and sharing were disabled, and any instructions to or confirmations from Flock Safety regarding deletion, export, or retention of the department's data after deactivation.

Please release all non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory exception for anything withheld. If any item is unclear, please contact me for clarification rather than denying it.

I request records in their existing electronic format (such as native exports, CSV, or PDF) delivered by email or download link. I do not request paper copies, printouts, or physical media such as CDs or flash drives. I am not requesting that new reports be created. Please do not refer me to an online transparency portal in place of producing these records.

I request a waiver or reduction of fees, as release of this information primarily benefits the general public by informing residents about the use of surveillance technology in their community. If charges will exceed $40, please provide an itemized estimate, including any less costly alternative, before work begins.

Thank you for your cooperation. I look forward to your prompt response, as required by the Texas Public Information Act.

Sincerely,
Blackland Prairie Records Project

title: Flock Safety / ALPR Surveillance Records – City of Newburgh

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Flock Safety / ALPR Surveillance Records – City of Newburgh
communications.communication:
Dear Records Custodian,

Under the provisions of the New York Freedom of Information Law (FOIL), N.Y. Public Officers Law §§ 84–90, I hereby request access to and copies of records held by the City of Newburgh, Orange County, relating to the planning, proposal, procurement, authorization, or attempted deployment of Flock Safety surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems.

This request is made in the public interest to better understand the use, consideration, or implementation of surveillance technologies by local government entities, including decision-making processes, vendor relationships, and potential impacts on public privacy.

The purpose of this request is to determine the origin, authorization process, procurement activity, proposed locations, and communications surrounding any surveillance camera system, including identifying which individual, agency, or vendor first initiated discussions or planning for such a program within the City of Newburgh.

Timeframe: January 1, 2023 – Present, including any earlier records referencing or relating to Flock Safety, automated license plate readers, or surveillance cameras within the City of Newburgh.

Records Requested

For the purpose of this request, the records I seek include, but are not limited to the following:

1. Contracts and Agreements

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, vendor agreements, procurement documents, or proposals involving the City of Newburgh and Flock Safety or any related entities concerning surveillance cameras, automated license plate readers, or related monitoring technology.

This includes draft contracts, executed agreements, amendments, pilot program agreements, trial program documentation, cancellation notices, procurement justifications, and contract termination records.

Legal Basis: Contracts involving public funds or public infrastructure are public records subject to disclosure under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87.

2. Records Identifying Project Initiation

All records reflecting the initial introduction, proposal, solicitation, or outreach regarding Flock Safety cameras or ALPR systems, including records identifying:

• the individual or office that first proposed or recommended the system  
• the first communications between the City and Flock Safety  
• vendor outreach to city officials  
• internal discussions about introducing the technology  
• marketing or sales outreach from vendors  

3. Internal Communications

All internal communications including emails, memoranda, text messages, chat messages, letters, meeting notes, or other correspondence among:

• the Mayor  
• City Council members  
• City of Newburgh Police Department personnel  
• City administrative staff  
• City legal counsel  
• Public Works or Planning Department personnel  
• other municipal offices  

that discuss:

• Flock Safety  
• automated license plate readers  
• surveillance cameras  
• camera deployments  
• vendor procurement or negotiations  
• surveillance technology adoption  

4. Communications With External Entities

All communications between the City of Newburgh and:

• representatives of Flock Safety  
• technology vendors or consultants  
• Orange County officials  
• local, state, or federal law enforcement agencies  
• regional intelligence or real-time crime centers  

concerning surveillance cameras, ALPR systems, or the Flock Safety program.

5. Vendor Demonstrations and Sales Outreach

All records relating to vendor presentations, product demonstrations, marketing materials, or sales outreach regarding Flock Safety or related surveillance technology, including:

• presentation decks  
• vendor proposals  
• demonstration scheduling emails  
• meeting invitations or call summaries  
• webinar invitations  
• follow-up communications  

6. Proposed Camera Locations and Site Selection

All records identifying, evaluating, or discussing proposed or potential locations for surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader systems within the City of Newburgh.

This includes but is not limited to:

• maps showing proposed camera placements  
• GIS maps or infrastructure maps  
• deployment plans  
• proposed installation locations or intersections  
• roadway monitoring points  
• entry or exit routes to the city  
• communications discussing site selection  
• vendor recommendations for placement  
• field surveys or site inspections  
• infrastructure or engineering assessments related to camera placement  

7. Deployment and Planning Documents

All planning or operational records relating to the surveillance system, including:

• deployment plans  
• camera location maps  
• infrastructure assessments  
• equipment specifications  
• installation schedules  
• operational capability descriptions  
• technology architecture documents  

8. Financial and Procurement Records

All records relating to funding, budgeting, or procurement of the surveillance system, including:

• invoices  
• payment records  
• purchase authorizations  
• budget allocations  
• grant applications  
• cost analyses  
• procurement justifications  
• financial approvals  

9. Meeting Records

All agendas, minutes, recordings, transcripts, or notes from City Council meetings, committee meetings, departmental meetings, or internal meetings where surveillance camera programs or Flock Safety systems were discussed, proposed, approved, or canceled.

10. Oversight, Audit, and Compliance Records

Any audit reports, legal opinions, compliance reviews, investigations, or internal analyses relating to surveillance camera programs or procurement processes.

11. Data Access, Sharing, and Integration

All records relating to data access or sharing involving the surveillance system, including:

• agreements allowing other agencies to access camera data  
• policies governing license plate reader searches  
• records concerning integration with regional surveillance networks  
• data retention policies  
• privacy or civil liberties assessments  

Electronic Records and Metadata

For all responsive electronic records, including emails and digital documents, I request that records be produced in their native electronic format where possible, including all available metadata and email header information.

This includes, but is not limited to:

• sender and recipient information  
• CC and BCC fields  
• full email header routing data  
• timestamps for sending and receipt  
• message ID fields  
• attachment metadata  
• document creation dates  
• last modified dates  
• author fields  
• file path information where available  

Providing metadata is necessary to determine the origin, timing, and authorship of communications relating to the surveillance camera proposal.

Request for Segregable Non-Exempt Portions

Should any portion of the requested records be deemed exempt from disclosure, I request the release of any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions in accordance with N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87(2).

Preservation of Records

Please note your obligation not to destroy or alter any records potentially responsive to this request. Once a FOIL request has been received, agencies are required to preserve all responsive records during processing.

Fee Waiver Request

I request a fee waiver for the processing of this request as the information sought is in the public interest and its disclosure will contribute significantly to public understanding of government surveillance programs and decision-making processes.

If potential fees exceed $200, please inform me before proceeding.

Public Availability of Communications

Please be advised that communications relating to this request, including incoming and outgoing correspondence, may be publicly published on transparency platforms such as MuckRock.com.

Statutory Response Time

As required under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 89(3), I look forward to acknowledgment of this request within five business days.

Sincerely,

Jordan Lassiter  
Independent Investigative Journalist
